title: Street marches and the slow New Orleans tempo
summary: Marches may have influenced jazz mainly through their slow tempo, suited to the hot climate; fast tempos are not original.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: What about the street marches, the funeral marches? Are they all the same thing?

In a way, that might have influenced jazz too, but I don't know. I would be hesitant to say that it actually had as great an influence as other things. Maybe the jazz influenced the street marches more than the other way around. Although, the fact that they were marches and had that definite beat in a lot of the marches are used as dance pieces. Well, of course, the obvious one is high society and a few others have been too. But, one thing you might notice in the street marches, which has relation to jazz, is the slower tempo. If you watch the high school bands here and especially other parts of the country down here too, now they go so fast you have to run with it to keep up with them. But the old time colored bands and the old time white bands too, as far as that goes, in general, just an old time New Orleans band on the street, goes along in keeping with the hot climate that we have. They don't like to hurry. They take their time. They really... And they do that in the jazz too. Any time you hear a real fast tempo, you can be sure that had nothing to do with the original New Orleans jazz. Because even things like Tiger Rag and those tunes, they didn't race them. They didn't, as they call it today, race horse music. They didn't do any of that. As far as we know, the old time New Orleans musicians. It was always a more relaxed feeling and slower. And that, of course, could have come from the slower marches, just in general, the slower tempo of life in the hot climate.
